Natural_Language: This part covers the policy and procedures for terminating contracts early and prescribes contract clauses and forms for termination.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_000_a: Part 49 covers policy and procedures for early contract termination; P_49_000_b: Part 49 prescribes contract clauses and forms for termination
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating scope coverage (a) and prescriptions (b). Conjunction appropriate as both define the part scope.

Natural_Language: This part covers the policy and procedures for terminating contracts early. The Government can terminate contracts for two main reasons: (1) For its own convenience; (2) Because the contractor failed to perform (called "default").
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_000_a_1: Government may terminate contracts for convenience; P_49_000_a_2: Government may terminate contracts for contractor default
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive: termination is for convenience OR default. These are the two exclusive termination bases.

Natural_Language: The Government can terminate contracts for its own convenience.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_000_a_1_a: Government has authority to terminate; P_49_000_a_1_b: Termination basis is Government convenience
Validation_Notes: Atomic: Government authority to terminate for convenience is a foundational principle of contract termination.

Natural_Language: The Government can terminate contracts because the contractor failed to perform (called "default").
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_000_a_2_a: Government has authority to terminate; P_49_000_a_2_b: Termination basis is contractor default (failure to perform)
Validation_Notes: Atomic: Government authority to terminate for default. Default defined as failure to perform.

Natural_Language: This part prescribes: (1) The contract clauses relating to termination and excusable delay; and (2) Instructions for using termination and settlement forms.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_000_b_1: Part 49 prescribes contract clauses for termination and excusable delay; P_49_000_b_2: Part 49 prescribes instructions for termination and settlement forms
Validation_Notes: Conjunctive: part prescribes both clauses AND form instructions.

Natural_Language: This part prescribes the contract clauses relating to termination and excusable delay.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_000_b_1: Part 49 prescribes contract clauses relating to termination and excusable delay
Validation_Notes: Atomic. Cross-references subpart 49.5 which contains the actual clause prescriptions.

Natural_Language: This part prescribes instructions for using termination and settlement forms.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_000_b_2: Part 49 prescribes instructions for termination and settlement forms
Validation_Notes: Atomic. Cross-references subpart 49.6 which contains forms and formats.

Natural_Language: Definitions used in Part 49.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_001_a: "Other work" means Government and commercial work the contractor is doing or plans to do, excluding work on the terminated contract; P_49_001_b: "Plant clearance period" means the period starting at contract completion/termination and ending 90 days after CO receives acceptable inventory schedules; P_49_001_c: "Settlement agreement" means a written agreement in the form of a contract modification settling all or part of a settlement proposal; P_49_001_d: "Settlement proposal" means a contractor or subcontractor proposal for ending a terminated contract, using required forms, counting as claims under false claims laws (18 USC 287, 31 USC 3729); P_49_001_e: "Unsettled contract change" means a contract change or term requiring a formal modification that has not been executed
Validation_Notes: Definitional section. All five definitions apply simultaneously. Settlement proposal definition notably includes false claims liability under 18 USC 287 and 31 USC 3729.

Natural_Language: Applicability provisions for Part 49.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_002_a: Applicability to contracts with termination clauses; P_49_002_b: Subcontract settlement requirements; P_49_002_c: Equitable adjustment authority; P_49_002_d: Settlement amount calculation method
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for applicability. All four subprovisions apply concurrently.

Natural_Language: Applicability of Part 49 to contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_002_a_1: Part 49 applies to contracts allowing termination; P_49_002_a_2: Part 49 does not apply to commercial product/service contracts under Part 12
Validation_Notes: Parent: both the applicability rule and the commercial exclusion apply together.

Natural_Language: This part applies to contracts that allow termination for Government convenience or contractor default. See part 13 for information on simplified acquisition contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_002_a_1_a: Part 49 applies to contracts with termination for convenience clauses; P_49_002_a_1_b: Part 49 applies to contracts with termination for default clauses
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive: Part 49 applies if contract has either convenience OR default termination authority. External dependency on Part 13 for simplified acquisitions.

Natural_Language: This part does not apply to contracts for commercial products and commercial services awarded under part 12 procedures. For those contracts, use part 12 for termination policies. This part can be used as guidance for those contracts, but only if it does not conflict with part 12 or the applicable clause.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_002_a_2_a: Part 49 does not apply to commercial product/service contracts under Part 12; P_49_002_a_2_b: Part 12 governs termination for commercial contracts; P_49_002_a_2_c: Part 49 may be used as guidance for commercial contracts if no conflict with Part 12
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]
Validation_Notes: Complex: exclusion from applicability with conditional guidance allowance. The conditional (Part 49 guidance only if no Part 12 conflict) uses implication. HIGH-RISK rule 15 flagged.

Natural_Language: Contractors must use this part to settle subcontracts terminated after a cost-reimbursement prime contract is modified, unless the contracting officer deems such a use inappropriate. The contracting officer must use this part as a guide when reviewing subcontract settlements. This applies when the contractor uses the subcontract settlement as basis for reimbursement under a cost-reimbursement contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_002_b_a: Contractors shall use Part 49 to settle terminated subcontracts under modified cost-reimbursement primes; P_49_002_b_b: CO may deem Part 49 use inappropriate (exception); P_49_002_b_c: CO shall use Part 49 as guide for subcontract settlement review; P_49_002_b_d: Applies when subcontract settlement is basis for cost-reimbursement reimbursement
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conditional: when subcontract settlement is basis for reimbursement, both contractor use and CO guidance apply. Exception for CO determining Part 49 use inappropriate. HIGH-RISK rule 15.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer may use this part to determine equitable adjustments resulting from a modification under Changes clauses. This does not apply to cost-reimbursement contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_002_c_a: CO may use Part 49 for equitable adjustments from Changes clause modifications; P_49_002_c_b: This authority does not apply to cost-reimbursement contracts
Justification_Rules: Addition (Add): Rule 8; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: "May" = permissive/discretionary (tautology). Explicit exclusion of cost-reimbursement contracts.

Natural_Language: When this part refers to the "amount" of a settlement proposal, calculate as follows: (1) Start with total settlement amount requested; (2) Subtract amounts due for completed work at contract price and amounts for settling subcontractor proposals; (3) Do not subtract credits from keeping/selling termination inventory or advance/partial payments already made.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_002_d_1: Start with total settlement amount requested; P_49_002_d_2: Subtract completed work amounts at contract price; P_49_002_d_3: Subtract subcontractor settlement amounts; P_49_002_d_4: Do not subtract termination inventory credits; P_49_002_d_5: Do not subtract advance or partial payments already made
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Calculation methodology: start amount, mandatory subtractions, and prohibited subtractions. The sequential nature of the calculation is preserved through conjunction and negation. HIGH-RISK rule 15 for the conditional deduction step.

Natural_Language: This subpart covers: (1) authority and duties of COs to terminate contracts; (2) post-termination requirements; (3) basic settlement procedures; (4) settlement agreements. More detailed rules in subparts 49.2, 49.3, and 49.4.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_100_a: Subpart covers authority/duties for termination; P_49_100_b: More detailed rules in subparts 49.2, 49.3, and 49.4
Validation_Notes: Scope provision. Conjunction of coverage areas. Cross-references to other subparts for detailed rules.

Natural_Language: Authorities and responsibilities for contract termination.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_101_a through P_49_101_f: Six subsections covering CO authority, termination conditions, no-cost settlement criteria, TCO responsibilities, small business preference, and fund release
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating six authority/responsibility provisions.

Natural_Language: Contract termination clauses give contracting officers the authority to: (1) Terminate contracts for convenience or default; and (2) Enter into settlement agreements under this regulation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_101_a_1: Termination clauses authorize CO to terminate for convenience or default; P_49_101_a_2: Termination clauses authorize CO to enter settlement agreements
Validation_Notes: Conjunctive: both authorities derive from termination clauses. Source authority for all termination actions.

Natural_Language: The CO must terminate contracts only when in the Government's interest. Use a no-cost settlement instead of termination when: (1) contractor will accept it; (2) Government property was not furnished; and (3) no outstanding payments, debts, or other contractor obligations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_101_b_a: CO shall terminate only when in Government interest; P_49_101_b_b: Use no-cost settlement when contractor will accept AND no Gov property furnished AND no outstanding obligations
Validation_Notes: Mandatory: "must" language. Conditional: all three conditions must be met for no-cost settlement to be used instead. HIGH-RISK rule 15 for the implication.

Natural_Language: Contracting officers should not terminate a contract for convenience when the remaining work is worth less than $5,000.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_101_c_a: CO should not terminate for convenience when remaining work < $5,000
Validation_Notes: "Should" = advisory, not mandatory. Threshold-based recommendation against termination for de minimis remaining work. PENDING_REVIEW due to "should" language.

Natural_Language: After CO or TCO issues termination notice, TCO handles settlement negotiations including no-cost settlements. TCO responsible for payment details. Auditors and TCOs must work quickly and give special attention to small business settlements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_101_d_a: TCO handles settlement negotiations after notice; P_49_101_d_b: TCO responsible for payment details; P_49_101_d_c: Auditors and TCOs shall work quickly; P_49_101_d_d: Special attention to small business settlements
Validation_Notes: Four concurrent mandatory duties. "Must" language for all elements.

Natural_Language: When same item under contract with both large and small businesses, and CO needs to terminate some undelivered items for convenience, CO must give preference to continuing small business contracts unless clearly shown small business unable to provide timely.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_101_e_a: Same item contracted with large and small businesses; P_49_101_e_b: CO needs to terminate some undelivered items; P_49_101_e_c: CO must prefer continuing small business contracts; P_49_101_e_d: Exception if small business clearly unable to deliver timely
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conditional preference for small business with narrow exception. "Must" = mandatory. "Unless clearly shown" = high burden to override preference. HIGH-RISK rule 15.

Natural_Language: CO handles releasing extra funds from terminations. This responsibility can be given to TCO if specified in writing.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_101_f_a: CO responsible for releasing excess termination funds; P_49_101_f_b: Responsibility may be delegated to TCO in writing
Validation_Notes: Default CO authority with permissive delegation to TCO. Written requirement for delegation. Cross-ref to 49.105-1.

Natural_Language: Notice of termination requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_102_a through P_49_102_d: General notice requirements, distribution, amendment, and reinstatement
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating four notice subsections.

Natural_Language: COs must terminate contracts only with written notice to contractor. See 49.601 for format. Notice may be expedited electronically with confirmation capability. When mailing, use certified mail with return receipt. If hand-delivering, get written acknowledgment. Notice must include: (1) reason for termination and contract clause; (2) effective date; (3) extent of termination; (4) special instructions; (5) employee assistance steps.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_102_a_a: CO shall terminate only with written notice; P_49_102_a_b: Electronic notice permitted if confirmation capability exists; P_49_102_a_c: Certified mail with return receipt required; P_49_102_a_d: Hand delivery requires written acknowledgment; P_49_102_a_1: Notice shall include reason and clause; P_49_102_a_2: Notice shall include effective date; P_49_102_a_3: Notice shall include extent (partial/complete); P_49_102_a_4: Notice shall include special instructions; P_49_102_a_5: Notice shall include employee assistance steps
Formal_Logic_Statement: P_49_102_a_a ^ (Electronic -> Confirmation) ^ (Mail -> CertifiedReturnReceipt) ^ (HandDelivery -> WrittenAck) ^ P_49_102_a_1 ^ P_49_102_a_2 ^ P_49_102_a_3 ^ P_49_102_a_4 ^ P_49_102_a_5
Validation_Notes: Multiple mandatory requirements. Written notice is absolute ("must"). Delivery method triggers specific requirements. Five mandatory content elements. HIGH-RISK rule 15 for delivery conditionals.

Natural_Language: The CO must simultaneously send the termination notice to the contractor; the contract administration office; and any known assignee, guarantor, or surety.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_102_b_a: CO shall simultaneously distribute notice to contractor; P_49_102_b_b: CO shall simultaneously distribute notice to contract admin office; P_49_102_b_c: CO shall simultaneously distribute notice to known assignee/guarantor/surety
Validation_Notes: Mandatory simultaneous distribution. "Must" language. All three recipient categories required.

Natural_Language: The CO may amend a termination notice to: (1) Fix minor mistakes; (2) Add information or instructions; or (3) Rescind if terminated items were completed/shipped before contractor received notice.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_102_c_a: CO may amend notice to fix mistakes; P_49_102_c_b: CO may amend to add information; P_49_102_c_c: CO may rescind if items completed/shipped before receipt
Validation_Notes: "May" = permissive (tautology). Three disjunctive grounds for amendment. Rescission ground requires factual predicate (items completed/shipped before receipt).

Natural_Language: Upon written consent of contractor, CO may reinstate terminated portion in whole or part by amending notice if determined in writing that: (1) circumstances clearly indicate Government still needs items; and (2) reinstatement benefits the Government.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_102_d_a: Contractor written consent required; P_49_102_d_b: Written determination required; P_49_102_d_1: Government still needs terminated items; P_49_102_d_2: Reinstatement benefits the Government
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: "May" = permissive even when all conditions met. Four conjunctive prerequisites: written consent, written determination, continued need, and Government benefit. HIGH-RISK rule 15.

Natural_Language: Settlement of terminated cost-reimbursement and fixed-price contracts may be effected by: (1) Negotiated agreement; (2) Determination by TCO; (3) Costing-out under vouchers using SF 1034 for cost-reimbursement (per subpart 49.3); or (4) combination. TCO should negotiate fair/prompt settlement; must settle by determination only when agreement not possible.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_103_a: Settlement methods are negotiation, determination, voucher costing, or combination; P_49_103_b: TCO should negotiate fair prompt settlement; P_49_103_c: Settlement by determination only when agreement impossible
Justification_Rules: Addition (Add): Rule 8; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive methods with preference hierarchy. "Should" for negotiation preference. "Must" for determination-only-as-last-resort. HIGH-RISK rule 15.

Natural_Language: After receiving termination notice, contractor must follow notice and termination clause. For convenience terminations, contractor generally required to: (a) stop work and stop placing subcontracts; (b) terminate related subcontracts; (c) inform TCO of special circumstances; (d) perform continued portion and request equitable adjustment if partial; (e) protect/preserve Government property; (f) notify TCO of legal proceedings; (g) settle subcontractor liabilities; (h) submit settlement proposal; (i) dispose of termination inventory.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_104_a: Stop work on terminated portion; P_49_104_b: Terminate related subcontracts; P_49_104_c: Inform TCO of special circumstances; P_49_104_d: Perform continued portion and submit equitable adjustment request if partial; P_49_104_e: Protect/preserve Government property; P_49_104_f: Notify TCO of legal proceedings; P_49_104_g: Settle subcontractor proposals; P_49_104_h: Submit settlement proposal; P_49_104_i: Dispose of termination inventory as directed
Validation_Notes: Nine conjunctive mandatory duties. All required concurrently after receipt of termination notice. "Must"/"required" language throughout.

Natural_Language: TCO duties after issuance: (a) must direct contractor actions, review proposals, negotiate settlement, settle by determination if needed; (b) may request specialized assistance; (c) should hold conference with contractor. Conference topics include settlement rules, extent of termination, continuing work, subcontractor termination, inventory management, accounting, proposal forms, financing needs, and timeline.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_105_a: TCO mandatory duties (direct, review, negotiate, determine); P_49_105_b: TCO may request specialist assistance; P_49_105_c: TCO should hold settlement conference with listed topics
Validation_Notes: "Must" for core duties (a). "May" for specialist requests (b) = tautology. "Should" for conference (c) = advisory. Conference topics are extensive (15 items) establishing best practices.

Natural_Language: TCO must estimate funds for settlement and within 30 days recommend release of excess funds. CO/TCO should quickly release initial excess. TCO must not recommend releasing under $1,000 unless CO requests. TCO must continuously monitor and promptly release additional excess. If previous releases create shortage, TCO must tell CO immediately; CO must restore within 30 days.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_105_1_a: TCO shall estimate and recommend excess fund release within 30 days; P_49_105_1_b: CO/TCO should quickly release initial excess; P_49_105_1_c: TCO shall not recommend release under $1,000 unless CO requests; P_49_105_1_d: TCO shall continuously monitor funding; P_49_105_1_e: If shortage from prior releases, CO shall restore within 30 days
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Multiple time-bound mandatory requirements (30-day windows). $1,000 threshold with CO override. Continuous monitoring duty. HIGH-RISK rule 15.

Natural_Language: For terminated construction contracts, the CO must direct cleanup actions to ensure: site cleanup, protection of usable materials, removal of hazards, and any other actions needed for a safe and healthy site.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_105_2_a: CO shall direct site cleanup; P_49_105_2_b: CO shall ensure protection of usable materials; P_49_105_2_c: CO shall ensure hazard removal; P_49_105_2_d: CO shall ensure safe and healthy site
Validation_Notes: Conditional on construction contract termination. All four cleanup duties mandatory when triggered. HIGH-RISK rule 15 but straightforward conditional.

Natural_Language: If the TCO suspects fraud or other criminal conduct related to the settlement of a terminated contract, the TCO shall discontinue negotiations and report the facts under agency procedures.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_106_a: TCO suspects fraud or criminal conduct; P_49_106_b: TCO shall discontinue negotiations; P_49_106_c: TCO shall report under agency procedures
Validation_Notes: Mandatory response to suspected fraud: both discontinuation AND reporting required. "Shall" = mandatory. HIGH-RISK rule 15 but clear conditional.

Natural_Language: Audit requirements for settlement proposals and subcontract settlements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_107_a: Prime contractor audit requirements; P_49_107_b: Subcontract settlement audit requirements; P_49_107_c: Contractor audit responsibilities; P_49_107_d: Audit report usage rules
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating four audit subsections. Cross-reference to Part 15 for cost or pricing data threshold.

Natural_Language: TCO must send settlement proposals to audit agency when value meets or exceeds certified cost or pricing data threshold in Part 15. TCO may send below-threshold proposals. When referring: include specific relevant information and facts. Audit agency must develop info, make reviews, and submit written comments. For sub-threshold proposals not needing examination, TCO does desk review with written summary.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_107_a_1: TCO shall send proposals at/above threshold to audit; P_49_107_a_2: TCO may send below-threshold proposals; P_49_107_a_3: Referral shall include specific info and facts; P_49_107_a_4: Audit agency shall develop info, review, and submit written comments; P_49_107_a_5: Sub-threshold desk review with written summary
Formal_Logic_Statement: (AtOrAboveThreshold -> AuditReferral) ^ (BelowThreshold -> (AuditReferral v ~AuditReferral)) ^ P_49_107_a_3 ^ P_49_107_a_4 ^ (~AuditReferral ^ BelowThreshold -> DeskReview)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Threshold-based mandatory audit with permissive below-threshold option. "Must" for at/above threshold. "May" for below threshold = tautology. Multiple HIGH-RISK implications.

Natural_Language: TCO must refer subcontract settlements to audit agency when: (1) amount exceeds certified cost or pricing data threshold; or (2) TCO decides accounting review advisable. Audit agency submits written comments. Does not remove prime/higher-tier responsibility for own accounting review.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_107_b_1: Subcontract audit required when exceeds threshold; P_49_107_b_2: Subcontract audit required when TCO decides review advisable; P_49_107_b_3: Audit does not remove contractor accounting responsibility
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive trigger for mandatory audit referral. Either threshold OR TCO judgment triggers it. Preservation of contractor responsibility is notable. HIGH-RISK rule 15.

Natural_Language: Prime contractors and subcontractors must perform accounting reviews and field audits. Government audit of subcontractor requested when: (i) competitive objection to upper-tier review; (ii) Government auditor already at location or more economical; (iii) consistency/orderly administration needs; (iv) contractor has substantial/controlling financial interest in subcontractor. Audit agency should avoid duplicating contractor reviews. TCO should ask audit agency to periodically examine contractor procedures.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_107_c_1: Contractors shall perform accounting reviews and audits; P_49_107_c_2: Government audit requested under four conditions; P_49_107_c_3: Audit agency should avoid duplication; P_49_107_c_4: TCO should request periodic examination of contractor procedures
Formal_Logic_Statement: P_49_107_c_1 ^ (CompetitiveObjection v GovtAuditorEconomical v ConsistencyNeeded v FinancialInterest -> GovtAudit) ^ P_49_107_c_3 ^ P_49_107_c_4
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Mandatory contractor audit duty with four disjunctive triggers for Government audit. "Should" for duplication avoidance and periodic exam = advisory. HIGH-RISK rule 15.

Natural_Language: Audit reports are advisory only. TCO uses them for negotiation or unilateral determinations. Government personnel must not reveal privileged information that could hurt negotiation positions. TCO may give audit reports to prime contractors and higher-tier subcontractors when appropriate and in Government interest.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_107_d_a: Audit reports are advisory only; P_49_107_d_b: TCO uses reports for negotiation/determination; P_49_107_d_c: Shall not reveal privileged information harmful to negotiation; P_49_107_d_d: TCO may share reports with contractors when appropriate and in Government interest
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Advisory nature of reports is critical. Prohibition on revealing privileged info is mandatory. Report sharing is permissive (tautology). HIGH-RISK rule 15.

Natural_Language: Settlement of subcontract settlement proposals.
Validation_Notes: Parent for seven subcontract settlement subsections.

Natural_Language: Subcontractors have no direct contract rights against the Government when a prime contract is terminated. Subcontractors may have rights against the prime or intermediate subcontractor. When prime terminated, prime and each subcontractor responsible for promptly settling immediate subcontractors.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_108_1_a: No direct subcontractor rights against Government; P_49_108_1_b: Subcontractors may have rights against prime/intermediate; P_49_108_1_c: Each tier responsible for settling immediate subcontractors promptly
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Critical privity doctrine: no direct Government-subcontractor relationship. Rights flow only through contractual chain.

Natural_Language: Convenience termination clauses require prime to terminate related subcontracts unless TCO directs otherwise. Failure to include proper clauses does not affect Government rights or increase Government obligations. TCO measures reasonableness by suggested clause amount; above-amount reimbursement only in unusual cases.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_108_2_a: Prime shall terminate related subcontracts unless TCO directs otherwise; P_49_108_2_b: Failure to include clauses preserves Government rights; P_49_108_2_c: Reasonableness measured by suggested clause amount; P_49_108_2_d: Above-amount only in unusual cases
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Government rights preserved regardless of contractor failures. Reasonableness standard tied to suggested clause amount. HIGH-RISK rule 15.

Natural_Language: Contractors settle with subcontractors using same policies as prime settlements. Government never pays lost anticipated profits or consequential damages. TCO must require inventory disposal per 52.245-1 and all settlements submitted for approval. TCO examines for necessity, good faith, reasonableness, allocability.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_108_3_a: Same policies for sub settlements; P_49_108_3_b: No lost profits/consequential damages; P_49_108_3_c: Inventory disposal per 52.245-1; P_49_108_3_d: All settlements for approval; P_49_108_3_e: TCO examines necessity/good faith/reasonableness/allocability
Formal_Logic_Statement: P_49_108_3_a ^ ~(LostProfits v ConsequentialDamages) ^ P_49_108_3_c ^ P_49_108_3_d ^ P_49_108_3_e
Validation_Notes: Absolute prohibition on lost profits/consequential damages. Four examination criteria conjunctive.

Natural_Language: TCO may authorize prime to settle subcontract terminations at $100,000 or less without approval. Requires written request, adequate procedures. Applies to all Executive agency primes. Annual minimum selective review. Revocation for inadequate procedures, improper settlements, or 2-year non-use. No proposal splitting.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_108_4_a: Authorization at <= $100K; P_49_108_4_b: Written request and adequate procedures required; P_49_108_4_c: All Executive agencies; P_49_108_4_d: Annual review; P_49_108_4_e: Three revocation triggers; P_49_108_4_f: No proposal splitting
Formal_Logic_Statement: (WrittenRequest ^ AdequateProcedures ^ Amount<=100K) -> (Authorization v ~Authorization) ^ P_49_108_4_c ^ P_49_108_4_d ^ ((InadequateProcedures v ImproperSettlements v TwoYearNonUse) -> Revocation) ^ ~ProposalSplitting
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Complex permissive authority with multiple safeguards. $100K threshold. Annual review mandatory. Three disjunctive revocation triggers. HIGH-RISK rule 15.

Natural_Language: TCO must treat final judgment against prime as settlement cost if allocable and five conditions met. If not all conditions met, TCO may allow fair portion. Arbitration awards treated same.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_108_5_a: Judgment as cost if allocable + 5 conditions; P_49_108_5_b: Fair portion if not all conditions; P_49_108_5_c: Arbitration parity
Formal_Logic_Statement: (Allocable ^ Cond1 ^ Cond2 ^ Cond3 ^ Cond4 ^ Cond5) -> JudgmentAsCost ^ (~AllConditions -> (FairPortion v ~FairPortion)) ^ P_49_108_5_c
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Five conjunctive conditions for full recognition. Permissive partial for incomplete conditions. Arbitration parity. HIGH-RISK rule 15.

Natural_Language: When prime inability to settle with sub delays prime settlement, TCO may settle with prime excluding sub proposal and reserving rights.
Atomic_Propositions: P_49_108_6_a: Delay trigger; P_49_108_6_b: TCO may exclude and reserve
Validation_Notes: "May" = permissive. TCO discretion to exclude delayed sub proposals. HIGH-RISK rule 15.
